5. SIFT Feature Extraction
SIFT (Scale-Invariant Feature Transform) is a powerful computer vision
technique used for feature extraction and matching in images. It is
particularly useful for tasks such as object recognition, image
stitching, and tracking.
5.1 Scale-Space Extrema Detection
SIFT starts by detecting keypoint candidates at multiple scales within
the image. This is achieved by applying a Difference of Gaussians
(DOG) operator to identify local extrema in the scale space. The DOG
is calculated by subtracting two Gaussian-blurred versions of the
image.
